html:
SMTO-PSM-0023 — A field in this connection parameter isn't filled in correctly

GUID: 66fb7a54-ef85-4030-8054-6826d3d87f63
Slug: typed-parameter-invalid
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • A connection parameter has a field that is empty, in the wrong form, or out of range, for example a port written as text. The message names the field. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the message to see which field is wrong, such as port, profile_version, redirect_uri or expires_at. SMTO checks each field separately, and the message names the first one that failed.
  2. Fix it on the parameter's Value tab. Write ports and version numbers as plain numbers without quotes, for example 443 not "443", and web addresses starting with https://. These fields must be a real number or a secure web address for the connection to work.
  3. If you're unsure what a field should hold, pick the matching template in the list next to New, select New, and copy your values into it. The template shows every field this kind of connection needs, in the right form.
  4. Keep passwords and tokens in their own fields, then select Save. SMTO keeps those fields hidden; putting secrets in other fields could expose them.

What success looks like

  • Parameter Store shows Saved and the connection parameter appears in the list.

If it still fails

  • If the same field keeps failing, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, without including any passwords or tokens.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Typed parameter validation rejected a field (wrong type, missing required value, out-of-range port, non-HTTPS endpoint, invalid expiry, account reference or TLS mode) for the selected profile template or database discovery request.

What this means

  • Typed profile validation rejects schema/type/range rules or semantic URL, account-reference, expiry, port or TLS-mode constraints. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Typed profile validation rejects schema/type/range rules or semantic URL, account-reference, expiry, port or TLS-mode constraints.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact field and semantic constraint, not just its JSON type.

How to fix it

  • The message names the field and rule (for example 'Typed parameter port: expected an integer', 'redirect_uri: required for web clients', 'expected an HTTPS endpoint', 'Unsupported sslmode'). Correct that field to match the template from src/agent_runtime/parameters/templates.py validate_typed (or the discovery request rules in discoverdb.py), keep secrets in their private fields, and save again.
  • Edit the identified field using the selected parameter template schema. Keep credentials in their dedicated private fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete intended profile passes both schema and semantic validation with private values kept private.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
